children: closed down 3.4% on Thursday after Bloomberg reported the company is moving to shield itself from rising expenses on its massive Project Jupiter data center being built in New Mexico, sending a notice citing force majeure to the project's developer.

said; the project has already hit serious setbacks, including the delay by New Mexico regulators of a key natural gas pipeline meant to feed the project.
The force majeure notice does not constitute an event of default on Oracle's

financing agreement, but even if the notice is intended as a precautionary step to win some wiggle room, it risks alarming lenders backing the project; debt tied to the development is already trading below 90 cents on the dollar, Bloomberg reported.
The news is "a logical follow-on to previously disclosed delays in powering the site," and by asserting force majeure now, Oracle

"positions itself to defer payments on capacity it cannot yet energize, should the campus fail to come online in 2028 as planned," William Blair analysts said in a note, maintaining an Outperform rating.
